scope: Root-accessible graphs, loops and coincident ports allowed; outdegree exactly two. Balanced subclass additionally requires indegree exactly two, counting port multiplicity.
equivalence: Rooted counts identify independent port swaps and root-preserving vertex relabeling. Unrooted shape counts additionally allow changing the starting vertex.
method: Filter all 203321 exact records, independently count indegrees, exhaust vertex permutations for every winning graph, and enumerate simple directed cycles. All-root scores are looked up by independently recomputed rooted canonical tables in the complete per-size dataset. Independently enumerate all ordered labelled transition tables through m=4 and match the complete balanced rooted class sets. Directly simulate each reported winning witness on every original static mask.
cycle_convention: Simple directed cycles use distinct vertices except the closing vertex, identify cyclic rotations, retain orientation, and ignore parallel-port multiplicity; loop port counts are reported separately.
limitations: No new full scoring run was performed. Completeness and exact scores through m=6 inherit the full exact-run certificate. This audit independently filters every record, checks winning witnesses/isomorphisms/invariants, and independently re-enumerates the strict balanced class sets through m=4. Winner multiplicity at m=5 is an observation, not a theorem explaining or predicting all maximizing classes.
deductions: The strict balanced subclass is not the same optimization problem: at m=3 its exact maximum is 5, whereas the unrestricted-outdegree-two maximum is 6.

At m=5 the five rooted maximizers comprise four directed unrooted shapes. Three rooted classes (a,b,c) lie in the strict balanced subclass and comprise two unrooted shapes; the other two have indegree multiset [1,2,2,2,3].
Every general maximizer through m=6 is strongly connected, but this finite observation does not justify imposing strong connectivity in the original search.

The unrestricted maxima equal m*(m+1)/2 through m=5; m=6 has maximum 23 greater than 21, including in the strict balanced subclass. A universal triangular upper bound is therefore false for these graph classes.

The four m=5 unrooted winning shapes have different simple-cycle length histograms. This certifies structural differences; it does not prove why all four tie at 15 or predict winner multiplicities at larger sizes.
